trust_decision.summary: At startup, getpath decides whether the interpreter is running from a source/build tree, which redirects stdlib_dir/prefix/exec_prefix to directories next to the executable. Before the fix, the presence of Modules/Setup.local next to the executable was accepted as a fallback build-tree marker when pybuilddir.txt was missing. The fix leaves pybuilddir.txt as the only marker. AT THE PINNED COMMIT THIS FIX IS ALREADY APPLIED.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names the Modules/Setup.local fallback in getpath.py. This is the CHECK FOR BUILD DIRECTORY block, and the pinned tree already has the post-fix comment '(gh-151544; CVE-2026-12003)' there.

fix_sites.entry_point: interpreter startup path calculation (python CLI / Py_InitializeFromConfig via getpath.py); BUILD_LANDMARK constant removed for posix and nt
fix_sites.module_kind: core startup config (frozen Python module run by C runtime)

fix_sites.entry_point: same; except-branch fallback to BUILD_LANDMARK removed
build: _bootstrap_python Makefile target now writes a dummy pybuilddir.txt

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Lib/sysconfig/__init__.py:222-228 (is_python_build still treats Modules/Setup or Modules/Setup.local under dirname(sys.executable) as a build tree; not touched by the fix)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: sysconfig.is_python_build only changes the paths reported for headers, Makefile and pyconfig.h (build/packaging metadata), not sys.path or stdlib loading, so a solver can argue it is not the code-loading sink the advisory names.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Running ./python out of an in-tree or out-of-tree build directory, and _bootstrap_python during the build, must still detect the build tree through pybuilddir.txt, including an empty file (IndexError branch) and the Windows PCbuild layout.

O6_input_shapes: posix BUILD_LANDMARK 'Modules/Setup.local' relative to the executable dir

O7_producer.where: Modules/getpath.py:496-540 writes config['_is_python_build'], stdlib_dir, prefix and exec_prefix, which Python/pathconfig.c:111 and Python/initconfig.c:197 consume

O8_uncovered_routes.route: sysconfig.is_python_build() / _PYTHON_BUILD still accepts Modules/Setup or Modules/Setup.local next to the executable as a build-tree marker, which redirects get_makefile_filename, get_config_h_filename and include schemes to that directory
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is build-metadata lookup used by packaging tools, not interpreter module search, so it is a different sink from the advisory's.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Lib/sysconfig package vs Modules/getpath.py; different language layer (stdlib vs startup)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Re-introducing a fallback build marker (e.g. Lib/os.py via BUILDSTDLIB_LANDMARKS) in the except branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That is exactly what the pre-fix code did; a maintainer wanting to keep source-tree runs working without pybuilddir.txt could plausibly add it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: config['_is_python_build'] > 0 forces build-dir detection even when home is set; a sibling could trust an env var to set it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The cross-build env vars (_PYTHON_PROJECT_BASE) already work this way in sysconfig.

O9_family: untrusted search path / build-tree marker spoofing (CWE-427)

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf/make with a C compiler (POSIX); MSBuild/PCbuild on Windows

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Drop the Setup.local branch in getpath.py and stop there, leaving sysconfig.is_python_build's Setup/Setup.local check unchanged.
